newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet down as winter demand eases.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet down as winter demand eases.

text.p: Singapore physical jet fuel prices eased slightly on talks that the winter demand from north Asia has ended amid a gradual build in supplies for late February lifting, traders said on Tuesday.
Traders said prices rose earlier on higher seasonal demand from Indonesia due to the Ramadan holidays and this has mopped up most of the available Singapore barrels for up to mid-February loading.

Indonesia may have bought up to 2.5 million barrels for February arrival with trades done at premiums of up to 70 cents above Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis and at 50 cents on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
Indonesia's purchases came at a time when most north Asian buyers have pulled out of the market as they have covered most of their winter needs, traders said.
But others said the market may rebound as the cuts to refinery runs in Singapore may lead to a further tightening of supplies and prices could spike if a new cold front develops in north Asia.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade for February swaps narrowed to $2.90/$3.10 per barrel against Monday's $3.10/$3.30.

The gas oil market was steady in the absence of any fresh indicators as sellers continued to offer large volumes but most were at relatively high prices of around $26.00 per barrel fob Singapore basis.

Offers for prompt cargoes loading in early February were offered to a low of $25.20 per barrel fob but no deals were confirmed. Buyers for second half February cargoes were at about $25.40 per barrel fob.
